Action Plan:
1. Emergency ambulance dispatched for suspected acute coronary syndrome; patient instructed to remain near open front door, stay on the line, and await paramedics.
2. Paramedics to perform on-scene ECG and transport to hospital for definitive evaluation/management of possible myocardial infarction.
3. Patient reminded to declare aspirin allergy (mild swelling) to all treating staff; hospital team to weigh risks/benefits of aspirin or alternative antiplatelet therapy.
4. Treating doctor to provide verbal hand-over to ambulance crew on arrival.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: New-onset chest discomfort while gardening a few hours ago; still present.  
• Symptom details:  
  – Quality: Diffuse pressure “like someone sitting on chest.”  
  – Location: Central chest.  
  – Radiation: Left arm and left shoulder.  
  – Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting), diaphoresis, shortness of breath, mild palpitations.  
  – Onset/trigger: Occurred during light gardening; no strenuous exertion.  
  – First episode; no prior similar pain.  
• Past medical history: Hypertension. No diabetes. Cholesterol status unknown.  
• Surgical history: Not discussed.  
• Medications: Not documented.  
• Allergies: Aspirin – causes swelling (mild allergic reaction).  
• Social history:  
  – Smokes ~10 cigarettes/day for 15 years.  
  – Alcohol: ~7–8 pints beer/week.  
  – Occupation: Restaurant (sushi shop) owner.  
  – Lives alone.  
  – Overweight (self-reported).  
• Family history: Father died of heart attack at ~60 y; mother with unspecified heart problems.

Objective:
• Video consult only; no vitals or physical examination performed.  
• No investigations yet; ambulance arranged for ECG.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Chest pain
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (rule-out myocardial infarction).
   - Differential diagnosis: Unstable angina, musculoskeletal chest pain, gastro-oesophageal causes, pulmonary embolism.
   - Investigations planned: Pre-hospital ECG; hospital cardiac work-up (serial troponins, cardiac enzymes, imaging) as per paramedic/hospital protocol.
   - Treatment planned: Emergency transport to hospital; consideration of antiplatelet therapy with caution due to aspirin allergy; standard ACS protocol per receiving facility.
   - Relevant referrals: Paramedic transport to emergency department; cardiology input anticipated.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Current medication list, full allergy list confirmation, baseline vitals, complete cardiovascular examination.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; suitable for extraction.
